messages:
marta: quick check — i'm about to update the API contract for 429/quota headers. proposal: keep Retry-After, add X-RateLimit-Bucket (route-level id), and keep X-RateLimit-Remaining/Limit/Reset. want to ensure per-route burst behavior is clear. any red flags?
kevin: +1 on keeping Retry-After. important for backcompat. question: should X-RateLimit-Reset be epoch seconds or ms?
sophie: epoch seconds is fine (matches other infra). prefer not to break existing "X-RateLimit-*" names. maybe add optional `X-RateLimit-Burst-Window`?
lee: for per-route bursts we track a sliding window; name it `X-RateLimit-Burst-Window` (seconds) is ok as opt-in. but we should document semantics: remaining counts are per-window not per-second.
marta: good call. i'll add burst-window as optional header. also need to decide streaming endpoints — we can't easily send 429 mid-stream. idea: preflight: if we detect we'd exceed quota send 429 before accepting and include headers; otherwise allow stream and apply graceful throttling. thoughts?
kevin: yep preflight check for streaming makes sense. fallback: if runtime runs out mid-stream, send a final chunk with an error frame and close. but try to avoid.
sophie: add a note to contract: clients should treat streams as "best-effort" and be prepared for truncated streams or an early connection close with reason header. include example header `X-Stream-Status: truncated`
anna: (brief) +1 for preflight. i'll add integration tests for the streaming case.
deploy-bot: deployed branch marta/429-contract-draft to staging — endpoint `/v1/generate` returns 429 with headers on quota hit
marta: nice. i'll update the contract PR and the docs page: https://docs.redwood.ai/api/rate-limits (will add examples). action items: 1) i'll update PR to include `X-RateLimit-Bucket` and optional `X-RateLimit-Burst-Window`; 2) kevin add epoch-second reset in runtime; 3) anna add e2e streaming test; 4) sophie update client guidance paragraph.
kevin: i'll also add unit tests to assert presence of Retry-After when bucket exhausted. will ping for CR.
sophie: small nit — in the 429 body we should return a compact machine-readable code, e.g. `{ "error": { "type": "rate_limit", "scope": "route", "bucket": "generate:short" } }` so clients can programmatically react.
marta: agreed. include that example in the contract.
lee: regarding rollover/backcompat: if a client only reads X-RateLimit-Remaining but not Burst-Window, behavior should be unchanged; burst-window is additive.
marta: perfect. thanks all. i'll land the PR today and tag y'all. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks — will review ASAP.
anna: thanks!
